_guide.purpose: Drives the in-app 'What's New' popup. After every release, add a new object at the TOP of `versions`.
rules: 2. Bump PATCH (1.0.7 -> 1.0.8) for bug fixes, PERF, security. Bump MINOR (1.0.x -> 1.1.0) for new features. Bump MAJOR (1.x -> 2.0.0) for breaking changes.
3. Every change is tagged to a module via `app`. The popup only shows a module to users who have access to it.

4. `app` must be a valid id from APP_ACCESS_CONFIG in assets/app.js (dpr, planning, quality, hr, masters, purchase, supervisor_app, ...). Use app: 'all' for platform-wide notes (performance, security, login) that everyone should see.
5. `type` is one of: feat | fix | perf | security | improvement. It renders as a coloured pill.
6. Keep each change one clear sentence written for a factory user, not a developer. No commit hashes.
7. `date` is the release date in YYYY-MM-DD.

versions.title: Machine-Wise Report — machines now in correct order

changes.text: In the Machine-Wise Plan Report, machines now sort in true numeric order (…-6, -7, -8, -10, -11) instead of text order that put -10 and -11 before -6.

versions.title: New Machine-Wise Plan Report
versions.summary: A new report shows every plan sitting on a machine, in queue order, exactly like the Machine Timeline — with live balance figures worked out up to the moment you open it. It comes in two views: a Summary (one row per plan) and a Detail (one row per colour). You can also tick a box to pull in the same OR's plans that are running on other machines. Open it from Reports, or straight from the Machine Timeline with the new 'Machine Report' button, and download it to Excel.

changes.text: New Machine-Wise Plan Report (Summary per plan + Detail per colour) showing OR/JC, mould, qty, live balance, start/end, expected end date, total plan time and queue position for every plan on a machine.
A 'Machine Report' button on the Machine Timeline opens the report directly, and an 'include same OR on other machines' option pulls in sibling plans. Both views download to Excel.

versions.title: Fixed DPR Compliance Summary showing a plan twice

changes.text: In the All-Factories view, a plan's hourly entries could appear twice in the Compliance Summary when the same order number existed in more than one factory. Each entry now shows only once.

versions.title: ERP data now updates itself every 5 minutes
versions.summary: You no longer have to press Fetch or Import. On the main server the app now automatically pulls the latest OR-JR Status, Summary and Details from the ERP every 5 minutes, imports them for every factory, and refreshes the Order Master — all on its own, with full history kept so you can check what happened. Factory (LOCAL) servers receive everything automatically and no longer show any upload or import buttons, because all master and order data is now managed only on the main server.

changes.text: The main server now auto-fetches ERP OR-JR Status, Summary and Details every 5 minutes and auto-imports them for every factory — no need to press Fetch or Import.
Order Master is rebuilt automatically after each ERP sync, and every run is saved to a history you can review (order changes are still tracked in the order completion history).

Factory servers are now read-only for masters and imports — all uploads and imports happen on the main server only and sync down automatically, so the upload/import buttons are hidden on factory servers.
Orders and OR-JR data stay fresh on their own, so planning always works from the latest ERP figures without a manual refresh.

versions.title: Fixed a duplicate-key error when importing planning data
versions.summary: Uploading a file or importing from ERP for a factory could fail with a 'duplicate key' error and import nothing, when a matching record was left under a different factory. The importer now clears the old record correctly, so the import completes and the data appears in Create Plan.

changes.text: Importing planning data (file upload or ERP) no longer fails with a duplicate-key error when a matching record exists under a different factory — the import now completes and the orders show up in Create Plan.

versions.title: Completed plans no longer come back
versions.summary: When a plan was marked Complete from the Machine Timeline on a factory server, it could reappear as active a few minutes later after syncing with the main server. The completion is now recorded correctly so it syncs to the main server and stays completed. Completions are also written to the plan history now, so you can see who completed a plan and when.

changes.text: A plan marked Complete now stays completed and no longer reappears on the board after a sync with the main server.
Completing a plan is now saved to the plan history, so you can see who completed it and when.

versions.title: Factory servers always use India time now
versions.summary: Dates, times and Day/Night shifts are now always calculated in India Standard Time on the factory servers, even if the computer's own clock or timezone is set wrong. This keeps DPR dates, shift timing and 'last updated' times correct everywhere.

changes.text: The app now forces India Standard Time (Asia/Kolkata) for all date, time and shift calculations, so a factory server whose Windows clock is on the wrong timezone no longer shows wrong dates or Day/Night shifts.

versions.title: Production & balance figures corrected across the app
versions.summary: On the main server, Produced and Balance could be badly wrong — a plan that never ran could show tens of thousands produced and a large negative balance. The cause: each factory reuses the same plan numbers (PLN-YYYY-NNNN), and the totals were adding up production from every factory that shared the number. Produced is now counted per factory, so the Planning Board timeline, Excel view, DPR Compliance Summary, shifting and reports all show the correct figures.

changes.text: Produced and Balance are now counted per factory, so a plan no longer shows other factories' production (which could make a not-started plan look massively over-produced with a negative balance).
DPR Compliance Summary production, OEE, efficiency and tonnage no longer inflate from other factories that reuse the same plan number.

versions.title: Orders with a cancelled job card show again in Create Plan
versions.summary: If an order had even one cancelled job card, the whole order disappeared from Create Plan — even when other job cards were still on schedule and moulds were left to plan. Orders now stay in the Create Plan list as long as they have at least one live job card; only orders whose job cards are all cancelled or completed drop off.

changes.text: A single cancelled job card no longer hides the entire order from Create Plan; orders with remaining live job cards and unplanned moulds now appear as expected.

versions.title: Correct Job Card number shows per plan on the board
versions.summary: When one order had several job cards (one per job plan), the planning board could show the wrong job card — or none — on a plan, because it picked any job card on the order instead of the one linked to that specific plan. Each plan now shows its own linked Job Card number.

changes.text: The board now shows each plan's own linked Job Card number (matched via the plan's link on the order), instead of an arbitrary job card when the order has more than one.

versions.title: Plan the same order & mould more than once
versions.summary: Create Plan used to block a second plan for the same order and mould while an earlier plan was still open, so you had to complete or cancel the first before splitting the work across machines or shifts. That block is removed — you can now create additional plans for the same order and mould. Over-planning is still limited by the remaining order balance.

changes.text: Removed the block that stopped a second plan for the same order and mould while an earlier plan was still open, so work can be split across machines or shifts.

versions.title: Rejected plans come back for planning
versions.summary: When a plan was rejected at the Moulding approval stage, its job stayed marked as planned and never returned to Create Plan, so it couldn't be planned again. A rejected plan now frees its mould and the job reappears in the Create Plan pending list.

changes.text: A plan rejected at Moulding approval now returns to the Create Plan pending list with its mould freed, so the job can be planned again instead of staying stuck.

versions.title: Planning board no longer goes blank when opened via a Create-Plan link
versions.summary: Opening the Planning board from a 'create plan' link could hit a script error that stopped the board from finishing drawing, leaving the Plan Qty and other columns blank. The board now loads fully in that case.

changes.text: Fixed a load-order error that could blank out the Planning board (including Plan Qty) when it was opened via a create-plan link.

versions.title: DPR Compliance Summary fully corrected for duplicated plan/hourly records
versions.summary: Follow-up to the previous fix. On the main server, entries could still appear multiple times when a plan record was duplicated. The Compliance Summary now uses a single plan record per entry, so each hourly reading shows once and production, OEE and efficiency are accurate regardless of duplicate plan or hourly records.

changes.text: Compliance Summary now uses one plan record per entry, so duplicate plan rows no longer repeat entries or inflate the totals on the main server.

versions.title: DPR Compliance Summary no longer double-counts duplicated hourly entries
versions.summary: When a factory server had duplicate hourly entries, the Compliance Summary was showing each reading several times and inflating the totals (production, OEE and efficiency read far too high). The report now counts each hourly entry once, so the entries, production, OEE and efficiency are correct even if duplicate records exist.

changes.text: Compliance Summary now counts each hourly entry once — duplicate synced records no longer repeat entries or inflate production, OEE and efficiency.

versions.title: Factory moulds now sync from the factory server up to the main server
versions.summary: Moulds added on a factory server now reach the main server correctly. Previously a factory's own moulds could fail to sync up and never appear on the main server for that factory, even though the factory server had them. They are now matched by mould number and factory, so each factory's moulds show on the main server.

changes.text: A factory's moulds now sync from its local server up to the main server instead of being dropped, so the Mould Master shows that factory's moulds on the main server.

versions.title: Auto-filled downtime hours can now be corrected with real production
versions.summary: When a machine has an ongoing quick-action (e.g. maintenance), the later hours are still filled in automatically — but those hours now stay open so a supervisor can enter the actual production that ran. Entering real output for an hour replaces the auto-filled downtime instead of being blocked by it.

changes.text: A quick-action entry no longer blocks the following hours — auto-filled hours stay selectable so you can enter the real production, which replaces the auto-filled downtime for that hour.

versions.title: Hourly production and downtime reasons sync reliably across servers
versions.summary: Hourly DPR entries and the downtime reason list now stay consistent between the factory servers and the main server, without rows clashing or going missing when the same record exists in more than one place.

changes.text: Hourly DPR entries now match up by a stable per-record id when syncing, so entries no longer clash or overwrite each other between the factory and main servers.
The downtime reason list now syncs by a stable per-record id, keeping reasons consistent across every server.

versions.title: New users now reach every factory server they're assigned to
versions.summary: A user created on the main server for one factory but given access to another factory now appears on that factory's server too. Previously the user only reached their home factory's server, so staff assigned to a different plant could not log in there.

changes.text: Users now sync to every factory server, so a person assigned to a factory can log in at that factory even if they were created under a different one.

versions.title: Order data syncs reliably between factory servers and the main server
versions.summary: Fixes a case where an order could repeatedly fail to sync between a factory server and the main server, leaving it out of date. Orders now match up by their order number, so they stay consistent everywhere.

changes.text: Orders no longer get stuck failing to sync — they are now matched by order number between the factory and main servers, so the same order stays consistent on both.

versions.title: Factory servers finish catching up after a sync stall
versions.summary: Clears a leftover notifications rule on factory servers that was stopping the sync from fully catching up, so a server that had fallen behind resumes advancing normally.

changes.text: Removed an outdated notifications rule on factory servers that could block the sync from fully catching up after a stall.

versions.title: Mould Master now shows only the selected factory's moulds
versions.summary: The Mould Master follows the factory you are logged into or have selected — it lists only that factory's moulds instead of every factory's. Superadmins on the main server can still choose 'All Factories' to see everything.

changes.text: Mould Master now shows only the moulds for the factory you are logged into or have selected; choose 'All Factories' to see every factory's moulds.

versions.title: Factory servers sync reliably again, and local backups keep working
versions.summary: A factory server that had stopped receiving updates from the main server now catches up and stays in sync. Automatic local backups also keep running even when the database has grown large.

changes.text: Factory servers that had stopped pulling updates from the main server now sync again — order/JR data resumes flowing instead of freezing.
Automatic local backups on the factory server now work even for very large databases, so a safety copy is always available.

versions.title: Mould Master fixes and correct Job Qty split when creating plans
versions.summary: The Mould Master now shows for every factory on the main server, and mould records can only be added or edited on the main server so the master stays consistent everywhere. On the factory servers the Mould Master is view-only and updates arrive automatically. When creating a plan across multiple colours, the Job Qty is now shared out correctly across the colours instead of piling onto the first ones.

changes.text: Mould Master now lists all moulds on the main server — it no longer shows blank for a factory whose moulds were saved under a different factory.
Mould Master can be added or edited on the main server only; on a factory server it is view-only and updates arrive automatically by sync.
Create Plan now divides the Job Qty across colour rows in proportion to each colour's quantity, instead of lumping it onto the first rows.

versions.title: DPR Avg Cycle Time now shows even when shots aren't entered
versions.summary: The Avg CT on the DPR Compliance Summary was showing a dash on machines where the shots count wasn't filled in. It now works out the number of shots from the pieces produced and the mould cavities, so the average cycle time always shows for a machine that ran.

changes.text: Avg CT no longer shows a dash when the shots field is empty — it derives the shot count from produced pieces ÷ cavity.

versions.title: DPR summary now shows Cycle Time and the average achieved
versions.summary: Every machine row in the DPR Compliance Summary now shows a CT line: the STD cycle time from the mould master next to the Avg CT the machine actually achieved (net run time ÷ total shots). If the machine is running slower than the standard, the average shows in red so you can spot it at a glance.

changes.text: Each machine row now shows Cycle Time — STD from the mould master and the Avg CT achieved (run time ÷ shots); a slower-than-standard average is highlighted red.

versions.title: More accurate Efficiency and OEE figures
versions.summary: Machine OEE and mould Efficiency now use the correct formulas, so the numbers reflect real shop-floor performance.

changes.text: OEE is now calculated correctly — rejected parts are no longer counted against the machine twice, so OEE and its Performance figure read accurately when there are rejects.
Mould Efficiency now measures against 23 productive hours per day (11.5 per shift), matching the Target PCS/DAY standard, instead of a full 24 hours — so efficiency percentages are realistic.

versions.title: Mould Master — cycle time now fills in output automatically
versions.summary: When you add or edit a mould, entering the Cycle Time (and cavities) now fills in PCS/HOUR and Target PCS/DAY for you, so the numbers are always consistent.

changes.text: In Add/Edit Mould, PCS/HOUR and Target PCS/DAY are now worked out automatically from the Cycle Time and number of cavities — for example a 40-second cycle with 1 cavity gives 90 pcs/hour and a 2070 daily target. You can still type over the values if needed.

versions.title: ERP reports — complete data, fetched centrally
versions.summary: ERP reports now show every row exactly as the ERP sends it — no more collapsed colour/mould lines — and all five ERP reports (JR Status, JR Summary, OR JR Details, BOM, Mould Item) are fetched once on the main server and shared automatically to every factory. Factory servers no longer contact the ERP directly.

changes.text: ERP reports now list every row the ERP returns — repeated colour or mould lines are no longer merged away, so nothing is hidden after a fetch and planned quantity adds up correctly.

ERP data is now fetched only on the main server and shared to every factory automatically; all five ERP reports (JR Status, JR Summary, OR JR Details, BOM, Mould Item) come down to each factory on their own, and factory servers never call the ERP directly.

versions.title: OR-JR Status — duplicate rows fixed
versions.summary: The OR-JR Status list no longer shows the same OR/JR twice. Rows left over from before a Job Card was issued are now cleaned up automatically, including on Factory 2.

changes.text: OR-JR Status no longer double-lists an order: leftover blank Job Card rows are removed once the real Job Card arrives, and spacing differences in the OR/JR number no longer split it into two.

versions.title: Tonnage Report — date-wise view and machine breakdown
versions.summary: The Tonnage Report now has a Daily (Date wise) option, and a Breakdown choice: see one total per date/period, or switch to Machine wise to break each period down by machine.

changes.text: Tonnage Report adds a Daily (Date wise) period and a Breakdown selector — Date wise only, or Machine wise for a per-machine split.

versions.title: Tonnage Report — Day / Night shift breakdown
versions.summary: The Tonnage Report can now split figures by shift. Choose Day & Night (Split) to see Good, Reject, and Overall tonnage separately for each shift, or Day Only / Night Only to focus on one shift.

changes.text: Tonnage Report now has a Shift filter: Day & Night (Split) breaks each period out per shift, and Day Only / Night Only filter to a single shift.

versions.title: Tonnage Report in Reports
versions.summary: A new Tonnage Report shows how much material you produced, split into Good, Reject, and Overall tonnage. Choose Weekly, Monthly, or Yearly and see the totals on top with a machine-wise breakdown below.

changes.text: New Tonnage Report with Weekly / Monthly / Yearly periods, showing Good, Reject, and Overall tonnage as a summary with a machine-wise detail table.

versions.title: Machine Monitor analytics: target, shift OEE, cycle spread, OEE trend
versions.summary: Four new analytics on Machine Monitor: Target vs Actual against the plan-board target, shift-wise OEE (Day vs Night), a cycle-time distribution histogram with % within tolerance, and a multi-day OEE trend to compare days.

changes.text: Target vs Actual, shift-wise OEE (Day/Night), cycle-time distribution, and a multi-day OEE trend added to Machine Monitor.

versions.title: More realistic OEE performance score
versions.summary: The OEE Performance score now uses a sustainable best cycle time (10th percentile) instead of a single fastest reading, so a one-off fast blip no longer makes efficiency look artificially low.

changes.text: OEE Performance now uses a realistic ideal cycle time, so efficiency reads correctly.

versions.title: Machine Monitor: OEE, efficiency and downtime analysis
versions.summary: Machine Monitor now shows OEE (Availability x Performance x Quality) with a breakdown, plus downtime analysis — total downtime, number of stops, longest stop and a list of downtime events. Downtime is inferred from when the shot counter stops advancing.

changes.text: New OEE / efficiency panel (Availability, Performance, Quality) and downtime analysis (total, stops, longest, event list).

versions.title: Machine Monitor redesigned — clean look + more analysis
versions.summary: The Machine Monitor now has a clean, light dashboard with more analysis: today's production, current rate, reject rate, active vs idle hours, output consistency, plus the hourly chart and cycle-time trend.

changes.text: Redesigned Machine Monitor with a clean light dashboard.
New analytics: current production rate, reject rate, active/idle hours and output consistency.

versions.title: Cycle-time stats ignore bad sensor spikes
versions.summary: Peak and average cycle time now ignore impossible values (over 10 minutes) that came from occasional bad sensor reads, so the cycle-time analysis shows realistic numbers.

changes.text: Cycle-time peak/average no longer include impossible spike values from bad reads.

versions.title: Machine Monitor: cycle-time analysis + a cleaner look
versions.summary: The Machine Monitor now includes a Cycle Time Analysis panel — peak, fastest and average cycle time, plus a trend line showing whether cycle time is rising or falling through the day. The page has also been given a cleaner, more polished look.

changes.text: New Cycle Time Analysis on Machine Monitor: peak / fastest / average cycle time and a trend line showing if cycle time is rising or falling.
Refreshed, more polished Machine Monitor visuals.

versions.title: Fixed inflated hourly production after a counter reset
versions.summary: Hourly production is now summed from real per-reading increments and ignores counter resets/jumps, so a machine counter resetting no longer shows a huge false spike for that hour.

changes.text: Hourly production no longer shows a false spike when the machine counter resets; it counts only real production.

versions.title: Machine Monitor — live per-shot log like the machine screen
versions.summary: A new Machine Monitor page shows a live per-shot log for each connected machine — one row per shot with cycle count, cycle time, fill, refill and positions — mirroring the machine's own PROC-1 screen, plus a live status header.

changes.text: New Machine Monitor page: a live per-shot log (cycle count, cycle time, fill, refill, positions) that mirrors the machine's own screen.

versions.title: Standard weight now matches the exact mould on the job
versions.summary: On the Supervisor and setup screens, the Article STD Weight (and other mould standards) is now taken from the exact mould on the job — for example '1595-TOP RING' — instead of a similarly-named base mould like '1595-TOP'. The weight you see now matches the Mould Master.

changes.text: The Article STD Weight now comes from the exact mould on the job, so a base mould with a similar code no longer shows the wrong weight.

versions.title: DPR scroll now keeps only the date bar and hour row frozen
versions.summary: On the DPR Compliance Summary, only the date bar and the hour-slot header row (07-08, 08-09 … Summary) stay frozen while you scroll. The filter row and the Plant Total summary now scroll away with the page, giving you more room to read the machine list.

changes.text: Only the date bar and hour-slot header stay frozen when you scroll the DPR Compliance Summary; the filters and Plant Total now scroll away.

versions.title: Standard weight and mould details now match the Mould Master exactly
versions.summary: The Supervisor and setup screens sometimes showed a standard weight (and other mould standards) that belonged to a different mould with a similar code. Mould details are now looked up by an exact mould number match, so the STD Weight you see matches the Mould Master.

changes.text: The Article STD Weight and other mould standards now come from the exact mould, so they match the Mould Master instead of a similarly-coded mould.
The mould name shown on the DPR is now resolved by an exact mould number match.

versions.title: Daily Production Report header now stays put while you scroll
versions.summary: On the DPR Compliance Summary, the date bar and the hour-slot header row (07-08, 08-09 … Summary) now stay frozen at the top as you scroll down the machine list, so you can always tell which hour column you are reading.

changes.text: The date bar and the hour-slot header row now stay frozen at the top of the DPR Compliance Summary while you scroll through the machines.

versions.title: ORJR Wise Summary and Detail can now be filled from the ERP
versions.summary: The Import from ERP Data button now works on ORJR Wise Summary and ORJR Wise Detail as well, not just OR-JR Status. No more downloading an Excel from the ERP and uploading it by hand. You still see every new and changed row before anything is saved, and only your own factory's orders are brought in.

changes.text: ORJR Wise Summary and ORJR Wise Detail can be filled straight from ERP data with the Import from ERP Data button — the Excel upload still works if you need it.
Only orders belonging to the factory you are logged into are brought in; orders from the other plants are counted and left out.
The review screen tells you how many rows were left out for having no mould number, so nothing disappears without explanation.
A large first import is brought in 5,000 rows at a time — confirm those, then press the button again for the rest.

versions.title: Machine production counter now reads correctly
versions.summary: Updated to the machine's corrected register map. The live production counter and cycle time now read correctly from the controllers — verified against a machine whose counter climbed as it produced.

changes.text: The machine's shot counter and cycle time now read correctly, so hourly production from the machine can be tracked.

versions.title: Removed the live-machines panel from the supervisor screen
versions.summary: The floating live-machines panel has been removed from the supervisor screen at the user's request.

changes.text: Removed the floating live-machines panel from the supervisor screen.

versions.title: Machine popup now shows produced, weight and average cycle — cleanly
versions.summary: The machine-counter popup on a DPR hour now shows pcs produced that hour, actual and average part weight, and current and average cycle time. Failed sensor reads are no longer stored as zero, so averages and counts stay accurate.

changes.text: Clicking the machine counter now shows pcs produced this hour, actual + average weight, and current + average cycle time.
A failed machine read no longer records a zero, which had made counts and averages look wrong.

versions.title: Machine data popup now shows shots produced per hour
versions.summary: Clicking the machine counter on a DPR hour cell now shows how many shots the machine produced in that hour (the counter's rise over the hour), plus the total counter and the real cycle time. Fields that this controller does not report accurately (cavity, shot weight) have been removed so only trustworthy numbers are shown.

changes.text: The machine-counter popup now leads with shots produced in that hour, and no longer shows fields the machine does not report correctly.

versions.title: Machine data now reads the live KEBA controllers correctly
versions.summary: First on-machine commissioning of the machine-data feature. The KEBA controllers send their values as decimals rather than the whole-number format the manual described, so counter and cycle time were decoded wrongly. This corrects the decoding (verified against the machine showing 205 shots at 33.9s), and makes the collector tolerant of controllers that only expose part of the register range.

changes.text: The machine counter and cycle time now show correct values instead of very large numbers, matching what the machine's own screen shows.

versions.title: Machines can now report their counter and cycle time to JMS automatically
versions.summary: Moulding machines with a KEBA controller can be connected to JMS over the factory network. Once a machine's IP is set in Masters, its shot counter and cycle time are collected automatically and shown next to the manually entered figures — so you can check accuracy before relying on it. Nothing is written into DPR automatically, so manual entry stays the record.

changes.text: A machine can now be linked to its controller by entering its IP address in the machine's settings, so JMS can collect live data from it.
Each hour cell shows the machine's own counter beside the entered figure; click it to see cavity, shot weight, cycle time and when the last reading was taken.
A live panel shows connected machines with their current counter, cycle time and running/stopped status.

versions.title: Weight checks widened to 10%, and the sync health alert now tells the truth
versions.summary: Supervisor weight tolerance moves from 5% to 10% and the DPR Compliance Summary flags parts that fall outside it. Behind the scenes, the hourly sync health check has been repaired — it had been failing on a connection fault for weeks while reporting it as a stale factory server.

changes.text: Part weight is now accepted within 10% of standard instead of 5%, so normal shot-to-shot variation stops being flagged as a problem.
DPR Compliance Summary now marks entries whose weight is over or under the allowed band, so out-of-spec parts stand out at a glance.
Import from ERP Data now shows the first 5,000 changes at a time — confirm those, then press it again for the rest. Very large first-time imports no longer risk failing part-way.
Searching OR/JR Status and Job Card reports now matches what you typed — the search was previously adding stray spaces and missing rows.
The automatic sync health alert works again. It had been failing to reach the server and reporting that as a stale factory server, which sent people to check the wrong machine.
When the health check cannot reach the server it now says so plainly, instead of blaming a factory sync it never managed to check.

versions.title: Set quantities can be corrected again, and the ERP import now covers every factory
versions.summary: Correcting the Plan Qty on a plan for a multi-piece set no longer fails with an 'exceeds the limit' error. The ERP import now brings in Factory 2's orders, which were being left out, and gets dates right. Job Card approvals can no longer half-save.

changes.text: Correcting a plan's quantity on a multi-piece set now works. Plan Qty is checked against that mould's own Mould Item Qty and Job Qty against the order's set quantity, so a 7-piece set ordered as 1800 sets correctly allows 10800 pieces on a 6-up mould instead of refusing it.
Quantity already planned is now counted per mould, so the body, lid and basket of one set no longer eat into each other's allowance.
The Edit Plan window shows both limits side by side — Mould Item Qty in pieces and OR Qty in sets — with the maximum allowed per colour for each.

A Job Card approval that fails now leaves the plan exactly where it was. Previously the plan could quietly move to the next stage while the screen reported an error, and a double-click could apply two approvals.
Factory 2 (Shivani) orders now come through the ERP import. They were being left out because the factory could not be matched by name.
Imported OR and Job Card dates can no longer land a day early or late.
The import preview now lists only the rows the save will really change, instead of reporting changes to remarks that were never applied.
Text arriving from the ERP is now displayed safely in the import review screen.

versions.title: OR-JR Status can now be filled from the ERP instead of an Excel upload
versions.summary: Masters -> OR-JR Status has a new "Import from ERP Data" button. It brings in JR Status data already fetched from the ERP, showing you exactly what is new and what changed before anything is saved. Only your own factory's orders are brought in. The Excel upload still works if you need it.

changes.text: New "Import from ERP Data" button on OR-JR Status fills the report from ERP data — no more downloading an Excel from the ERP and uploading it by hand.
The import only brings in orders belonging to the factory you are logged into; orders from the other plants are counted and left out.
Before saving, you see the same review screen as the Excel upload, listing every new and changed row so nothing is written without you approving it.
The screen shows when the ERP data was last fetched, and warns you if it is more than a day old so you can ask a superadmin to refresh it.
A blank Remarks value can no longer wipe the Remarks already saved against an order — this applies to the Excel upload as well.

versions.title: Plan approvals no longer fail on the factory server
versions.summary: Approving a plan on a factory (LOCAL) server could fail with a database duplicate-key error, leaving the plan stuck in Pending Plan Approval. The server now keeps its internal record numbering in step with records received from the main server.

changes.text: Approving a plan from Pending Plan Approval no longer fails with a duplicate-key error on factory servers — the approval saves and the plan moves on as expected.
Factory servers now re-align their internal record numbering after receiving data from the main server, preventing duplicate-record errors when saving new entries.

versions.title: Job Card approval can no longer be skipped from the Machine Timeline
versions.summary: Marking 'JC Given', setting a P1-P4 priority, or starting a plan now always requires a linked Job Card that has been approved by both PPC and Moulding. Removing JC Given or clearing a priority still works as before.

changes.text: 'JC Given' can only be ticked after a Job Card is linked and both PPC and Moulding have approved the plan — the box stays greyed out until then.
Setting a machine priority (P1-P4) or starting a plan is blocked until the Job Card approval is complete, with a message telling you which approval is still pending.
Priorities that were already set earlier keep working; only new assignments need the completed approval.

versions.title: Fix: changing a plan's mould now works even when the correct mould is already planned
versions.summary: In the superadmin Edit Plan window, correcting a plan to a mould that is already planned for the same OR used to show an error. It now applies cleanly.

changes.text: Edit Plan: you can now correct a plan to a mould that is already planned for the same OR without getting an error.

versions.title: New Machine Maintenance Report — see which machines lose the most hours to maintenance
versions.summary: Reports gets a Machine Maintenance Report: pick Daily, Weekly or Monthly and a date range, and see machine-wise maintenance downtime in hours, with the most-affected machines highlighted on top. Exports to Excel/CSV.

changes.text: New Machine Maintenance Report: choose Daily, Weekly or Monthly and a date range to see maintenance downtime machine-wise, in hours and minutes.
A summary on top shows total maintenance downtime, how many machines were affected, and each machine's total — most-affected machines first.
Counts maintenance from both supervisor quick actions and downtime reasons logged inside production entries, so nothing is missed.

versions.title: DPR now predicts each shift's final tonnage — per machine, per line, and plant-wide
versions.summary: While a shift is running, the Compliance Summary shows how many pieces and how many kg each machine is expected to finish with by shift end, based on its actual speed so far. Line headers and the Plant Total card show the same prediction added up.

changes.text: Each machine's summary box now shows a Pred line — the pieces and kg that machine is expected to reach by the end of the selected shift, based on its actual speed so far (or the standard rate if the shift just started).
Every line header shows the predicted total kg for that line, and the Plant Total card at the top gets a new Pred. Tonnage figure for the whole plant.
The prediction respects maintenance windows and completed moulds — those hours are not counted — and it only appears while the shift still has hours left.

versions.title: PPC can now allow extra production beyond the 10% limit — with a full record of who allowed what and why
versions.summary: When a colour hits its 10% over-production block, PPC/Planner/Admin can allow extra quantity for that colour from the Machine Timeline, with a written reason. Supervisors see who allowed the extra, and a new report lists every allowance.

changes.text: In the Machine Timeline colour view, PPC managers, planners and admins get a new Allow button to permit extra quantity for a colour beyond the 10% cap — a reason is compulsory.
The colour table shows how much extra was allowed and by whom, with the reason on hover, plus the full history of earlier allowances.
When PPC allows extra quantity for a colour, the entry limit increases automatically and the colour table shows a badge with the allowed extra and the name of who allowed it.
The over-production block message now tells the supervisor to ask PPC for extra allowance from the Machine Timeline, instead of a dead end.

New report: Extra Allowed QTY By PPC — every allowance with who allowed it, against which order/job/plan, which colour, how much, and the written reason, with totals per person and per colour. Exports to Excel/CSV.

versions.title: Job Detail gets a trend chart, and machines that go quiet raise an alert
versions.summary: The DPR Job Detail window is redesigned with a progress ring, an hourly trend chart with target line and estimated finish time, and over-produced quantities are now shown instead of a zero balance. The Compliance Summary warns when a machine has no entry for the last 3 hours.

changes.text: When a colour is produced above its plan, the Balance column now shows how many pieces OVER it went (in blue) instead of showing 0.
New hourly Production Trend chart in the Job Detail window — produced, rejected and downtime per hour, with the target rate line and day/night markers.
The Job Detail window now predicts when the job will finish, based on the last few hours' actual speed, and warns when the machine is running behind target.
The Job Detail window has a cleaner look: a progress ring, clear stat tiles, and pie charts for downtime and rejection reasons.

The Compliance Summary shows a red alert when a machine has had NO production entry for the last 3 hours — with a banner on top, a blinking mark on the machine row, and a small popup with that machine's colour-wise production while you scroll.

Every machine row now shows small badges when that machine did a Mould Change (yellow MC), Colour Change (orange CC) or Job Change (blue/red JC) — so changes are visible at a glance without opening entries.

versions.title: Downtime on production hours now shows as a split box

changes.text: When a production hour also has supervisor downtime, the box now splits in two — quantity and colour on top, the downtime reason with its minutes in a coloured strip below, instead of the small badge that was hard to read.
Downtime reasons that don't have their own signboard colour now show in a neutral grey strip with the minutes, instead of plain pink hours.

versions.title: Maintenance hours are now yellow, like the factory signboard

changes.text: Machine Maintenance hours in the Compliance Summary are now yellow with the maintenance tools icon — the same colour as the signboard on the machine.
Every downtime reason now shows its icon inside a small round sign, so the grid reads like the boards on the shop floor.
When an hour has both production and a short downtime, the box now splits in two — quantity on top and the downtime reason with its minutes below, easy to read without opening the entry.

versions.title: Supervisor entry checks stop over-count and wrong setup values
versions.summary: The Supervisor app now guards production entry: cavity can't exceed the mould's standard, article weight must stay within ±5% of standard, and colour-wise entry is capped at 10% over the planned quantity so a colour can't be over-produced.

changes.text: Actual Cavity can no longer be saved higher than the mould's Standard Cavity.
Actual article weight must be within ±5% of the standard weight — the allowed range is shown if an entry is outside it.

Colour-wise production is capped at 10% over that colour's planned quantity: a colour planned for 500 can take at most 550 across all entries, and the colour picker shows how many more pieces are allowed.
When a colour reaches its limit the app explains it clearly instead of showing a confusing zero, and unplanned colours are left uncapped.

versions.title: See why a machine was down right on the DPR summary
versions.summary: The DPR Compliance Summary now shows an icon and name for every downtime reason, and hour slots that had both production and downtime show a small badge with the reason and minutes — no need to open the entry.

changes.text: Machine Maintenance, Manpower Shortage, No Plan, Mould Maintenance and Mould Trial hours now show a clear icon with the reason name in the summary grid.
When an hour has production and downtime together, the slot shows a small badge with the downtime reason and minutes — point at it to see the full breakup.
The filter bar shows a legend of the new reason icons, and the View Filter list shows matching symbols.

versions.title: Supervisor app updates itself and never blocks your taps
versions.summary: The Supervisor app now picks up new fixes on its own, and the Processing popup can always be dismissed with one tap.

changes.text: The app now checks for updates on its own and refreshes itself when a fix is released — no need to close and reopen it. It never refreshes while you are typing an entry.
Tapping the Processing popup now always dismisses it — it can no longer jump straight back onto the screen.

versions.title: Sync alerts now name the factory that stopped syncing
versions.summary: Behind the scenes: when a factory's local server stops sending data to the main server, the automatic alert email now says exactly which factory it is and for how long — so the problem gets fixed faster.

changes.text: Sync health alert emails now name the exact factory server that stopped syncing and how long ago its last update was, instead of a generic warning.
The alert also tells apart a stopped factory server from the main server being down, so the right thing gets checked first.

versions.title: Supervisor submit no longer gets stuck on Processing
versions.summary: Submitting a DPR entry on the Supervisor app no longer leaves the Processing popup stuck on screen — you see Saved right away and can move to the next hour.

changes.text: After tapping Submit DPR, the Processing popup used to stay stuck for 15–30 seconds on slow Wi-Fi. It now closes as soon as the entry is saved.
Background checks after a save no longer freeze the whole screen — the setup card shows its own small Checking message instead.
If the network is too slow to confirm a save, the app now tells you clearly to check the slot list before submitting again, instead of showing a technical error.

versions.title: Machine queue follows your P1-P4 priority
versions.summary: The plan order you set with P1-P4 priorities now drives the schedule everywhere — card order, dates, and the Mould Change Report all tell the same story.

changes.text: Machine Timeline dates now follow the P1-P4 priority order you set on plans, so the card shown second also runs second — no more dates jumping between cards.
Excel View Timeline now uses the same realistic expected-finish chaining as the Machine Timeline.
The Mould Change Report detects changes in the same priority order, so its times and the timeline's Mould Change badges always agree.

versions.title: Mould change day runs 8 AM to 8 AM
versions.summary: The Mould Change Report now follows the factory day, and timeline cards spell out Mould Change clearly.

changes.text: Selecting a date in the Mould Change Report now shows every change from 8:00 AM that day to 8:00 AM the next morning, so early-morning changes are no longer missing from today's sheet.
Machine Timeline and Excel View Timeline cards now say 'Mould Change' in full instead of the short code 'CHG'.

versions.title: Faster, safer DPR entry on the supervisor screen
versions.summary: No more double entries from double-taps or weak WiFi, Fill DPR now lands on the colour picker first, and the job list refreshes without freezing the screen.

changes.text: Tapping Submit twice, or a weak WiFi retry, can no longer save the same hour's entry two times.
The Submit button greys out while saving and comes back on its own, so a failed save can always be retried.
Fill DPR now scrolls to the Colour Breakdown so you pick the colour first before entering data.
The job list refreshes in the background — the screen no longer freezes with a full-screen Processing message.

versions.title: Better Daily Mould Change Report
versions.summary: The Mould Change Report is now a complete, print-ready sheet with accurate times, serial numbers, signatures and an Excel download.

changes.text: The Mould Change Report now shows correct realistic times even when opened directly, without visiting the Machine Timeline first.
The report is a proper daily sheet: company header, serial numbers, and a signature section for PPC, the mould change team, and the production head.
Printing now repeats the column headings on every page and never splits a row across two pages.
New Excel button downloads the loaded report as a spreadsheet.

versions.title: Realistic machine schedule and mould change times
versions.summary: The Machine Timeline and Mould Change Report now follow the machine's real production speed, so upcoming plans and mould changes show realistic dates instead of standard-speed estimates that could already be in the past.

changes.text: Queued plans on the Machine Timeline now start from the previous plan's expected finish (based on actual balance quantity), so a slow-running plan pushes the whole queue to realistic dates.
The Daily Mould Change Report shows mould change times that match the Machine Timeline, so the printed sheet no longer lists changes at times that have already passed.

versions.title: Correct a plan after it's created
versions.summary: Superadmins can now fix the quantity and colour breakdown of a plan that was already created, without deleting and re-making it.

changes.text: Superadmins get an Edit Plan button on each plan to correct the quantity and per-colour breakdown after the plan was created; every change is logged.

versions.title: Smoother, lighter interface
versions.summary: Removed heavy background effects so pages feel snappier, especially when scrolling large tables.

changes.text: Stopped a constantly-animating page background that was quietly slowing down every screen.
Made scrolling through big tables smoother by simplifying row hover and scrollbar styling.

versions.title: Reliable menu on phones & tablets
versions.summary: The side menu now slides in from a hamburger button on phones, tablets, and zoomed-in screens instead of disappearing.

changes.text: The side menu no longer vanishes on small screens or when the page is zoomed in — tap the menu button at the top-left to slide it open.
Tap the dimmed area or press Escape to close the menu; pages now scroll normally with the bottom bar in place.

versions.title: Security hardening
versions.summary: Removed credentials that were accidentally stored in the app's code and tightened protections so it can't happen again.

changes.text: Removed database and service passwords that were accidentally saved inside the application files.
Backup and maintenance tools now ask for the database password instead of storing it.

versions.title: Faster page loads (fix)
versions.summary: Fixed the faster app scripts not building on the live server.

changes.text: Fixed the smaller app script not being generated during the live build, so pages now load correctly and faster.

versions.title: Faster page loads (part 2)
versions.summary: Pages now serve the smaller, faster app scripts everywhere — including on the live server.

changes.text: Pages now load the minified app script, so every screen loads faster on all servers.

versions.title: Faster page loads
versions.summary: Pages now load quicker and work fully offline on the factory server.

changes.text: Made the app scripts smaller so pages load faster, especially on slower connections.
Fonts and the logo now load from our own server — no outside downloads, so the app is faster and works offline.

versions.title: ORJR Wise Summary row delete
versions.summary: You can now remove individual rows from the ORJR Wise Summary, just like the ORJR Wise Detail view.

changes.text: Added a delete button on each ORJR Wise Summary row so you can remove a single row you no longer need.

versions.title: What's New notifications
versions.summary: The app now tells you exactly what changed after every update — tailored to the modules you use.

changes.text: After every update, a 'What's New' popup shows the changes for the modules you have access to.
Click the version number at the bottom of the sidebar any time to re-read the latest release notes.

versions.title: Stability & Quality
versions.summary: Fixes across the Daily Production Report and Quality modules, plus a supervisor entry fix.

changes.text: Fixed the Daily Production Report crashing and showing a blank page.
Corrected reports that were showing zero target and zero efficiency.
Compliance View filter now correctly includes machines stopped for MP Shortage, Maintenance and other downtime reasons.
Fixed First Piece Approval (FPA) images not displaying.
Added new panels to the Quality Dashboard for a clearer at-a-glance view.
Cleaned up unused screens for a faster, tidier module.
Stopped the quick-action auto-fill from carrying forward after you make a manual Main entry.

versions.title: Planning & Supervisor upgrades
versions.summary: New Planning tools, a redesigned supervisor entry experience, and automatic factory-server updates.

changes.text: Added a High Priority Job Sheet to the Planning Board.
New Recent Slots panel to quickly reopen your recent entries.
Redesigned entry cards with clearer type badges and better layout on mobile.
Fixed reject/downtime chips and the header Line chip overflowing on small screens.
Factory local servers now update themselves automatically from the main server.
New Activity Monitor shows real-time user activity across all JMS Ocean apps.

versions.title: Performance & QC redesign
versions.summary: A major speed-up across the platform and a refreshed Quality Control experience.

changes.text: Made pages load noticeably faster by fixing slow database queries and adding indexes on hot paths.
Hardened session handling with secure random session IDs.
Redesigned QC with compact cards, a machine-sorted queue, and a mandatory FPA -> Setup -> QC flow.
Added an image gallery and verify-from-queue for faster inspections.
